figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Functional characterization of TmCYP1. (A) Feeding experiments using 1 as substrate. (i) Enzymatic conversion of 1 to 1β-
dehydroxybaccatin IV (1a) and baccatin I (1b) by N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of TmCYP1. The TmCYP1 was not able to
transform 1b to 1a in N. benthamiana transient expression system; (ii) HPLC chromatograms (227 nm) of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves
with transient expression of (a) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-TmCYP1+1; (b) pEAQ-HT-DEST1+1; (c) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-TmCYP1+1b; (d) pEAQ-HT-DEST1
+1b, and (e) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-TmCYP1. (B) Feeding experiments using 2 as substrate. (i) Enzymatic conversion of 2 into 5α-deacetylbaccatin I
(2b) by N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of TmCYP1. Expression of TmCYP1 combined with CYP725A4 did not yield 2a; (ii) HPLC
chromatograms (227 nm) of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of (a) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-TmCYP1+2, (b) pEAQ-HT-
DEST1-TmCYP1+pEAQ-HT-DEST1-CYP725A4+2, (c) pEAQ-HT-DEST1+2, and (d) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-TmCYP1, respectively. HPLC-MS analyses
were shown in Supplementary Figures S6–S8. The Figures in brackets represent conversion.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Isotopic labelling experiments. (A) C5-acetyl 2H-labelled 1. (i) Enzymatic conversion of (5-OAc-d3)-1 into (4-OAc-d3)-1a and (5-OAc-d3)-1b
by N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of TmCYP1; (ii) Partial 1H NMR spectra of the labelled and unlabelled products, deuterium-
labelled (4-OAc-d3)-1a and (5-OAc-d3)-1b from (5-OAc-d3)-1. (B) C5-acetyl-18O labelled 1. (i) Enzymatic conversion of (5-Ac-18O)-1 into (4-18OAc)-1a
by N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of TmCYP1, the hexa-ols product (1c) was obtained using sodium methylate; (ii) Extracted ion
chromatograms (EIC) and high resolution ESI mass spectra of the unlabelled 1c compared with that of the labelled (4-18O)-1c. The chemical
syntheses of (5-OAc-d3)-1 and (5-Ac-18O)-1 were described in experimental procedures 12 and 16 of Supporting Information.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. DFT calculations for the oxetane ring formation. (A) Reaction mechanism; (B) Calculated free energy profiles for the intermediates and
transition-state structures. Free energy profile in kcal/mol. Spin multiplicity=2: P1 can be directly generated from N1 in a barrier-free manner. S
atom is from a Cysteine residue of enzyme (TmCYP1). The S atom from the Cysteine residue is treated with proton saturation (� SH) in the
simplified active site model.[40]

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Exploring the substrate scope of TmCYP1. (A) The chemical structures of substrate used to explore for substrate scope of TmCYP1. (B) (i)
Enzymatic conversion of 3 and 3a by N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of TmCYP1, T7βOH and TmCYP1+T7βOH; T7βOH: taxoid
7β-hydroxylase. (ii) HPLC chromatograms (227 nm) of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves with transient expression of (a) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-
TmCYP1+3, (b) pEAQ-HT-DEST1+3, (c) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-T7βOH+3a, (d) pEAQ-HT-DEST1+3a, (e) pEAQ-HT-DEST1-T7βOH+3, (f) pEAQ-
HT-DEST1-T7βOH+TmCYP1+3, (g) TmCYP1 and (h) T7βOH.
